brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: Two Hex base · Full cells (0,0,0) and (1,0,0) joined by a joint bolt. Each cell carries a Keyhole hanger (hex-acc-keyhole) on slot 2, the wall-side face. check_build reports meshClash 'clear' and no rule errors. I chose slot 2 as the wall side on the assumption that it lies flush against the wall; the tool does not confirm wall orientation, so this should be checked against the real wall.
Two Hook plates (hex-acc-hook), each carrying two hooks, on slot 5 of both cells, the front faces opposite the keyhole hangers. Mesh check is clear.

finish.summary: A two-cell wall rack: two full hex bases joined by one joint bolt, with a keyhole hanger on each cell's wall-side face and a hook plate on each cell's front face (four hooks total). Mesh check is clear with no rule errors. Remaining notes: the cells are not yet closed with covers or caps (informational only), and the wall-side orientation of the keyhole faces is my assumption, not something the configurator verifies.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Keyhole hangers and hook plates are both in the catalog. I'll check where accessories can attach to the single base cell.
The base cell has accessory faces 0 to 3. I'll add a second base cell next to it, then put keyhole hangers on the back face of each cell and see whether the configurator accepts them.
